column1: # sentenceSoFar ends mid-word (the partial word being typed) OR with a
# trailing space (nothing typed yet — pure next-word prediction). The
# runner splits it into (context = last *completed* word, prefix = partial
# word) exactly like CodeKeyboardIME does at suggestion time.
# expected accepts multiple pipe-separated alternatives — real language
# often has several reasonable next words ("I am looking " -> forward,
# towards, at are all fine), so a case passes if ANY listed alternative
# Trailing-space cases are the ones that actually exercise the bigram
# model — typing the full previous word and asking "what comes next with
# nothing typed" is the real value of autocomplete. A case where the
# expected word is already fully spelled out except its last couple
# letters (e.g. "please let me kno") tests almost nothing: the trie prefix
# search alone narrows it to a handful of candidates regardless of context.
#   next-word          — trailing space, single-word context (what the
#                        production bigram model actually uses today)
#   next-word-phrase    — trailing space, but the *correct* answer really
#                        depends on 2+ words of context. The model only
#                        sees the last word, so these are expected to
#                        expose a real coverage gap, not pass today.
#   prefix              — partial word typed, trie-only, short/no useful
#   prefix+context      — partial word typed, where bigram context could
# ── next-word: single-word context, verified against bigrams.json seed ──
# ── next-word-phrase: correct answer needs more than the last word ───────
# these are expected to fail today — the model only sees "me"/"you"/"the",
# not "let me"/"thank you"/"the same" — documenting exactly where a
# 1-word bigram context runs out of signal.
# ── prefix: partial word typed, trie-only, short/no useful context ───────
# ── prefix+context: partial word typed, context could disambiguate ───────
